land.text: Dyfed incorporated by Hywel Dda 'Through his marriage to Elen' into the enlarged realm of Deheubarth

correction.text: Dyfed 'based on the former territory of the Demetae' bordered by the rivers Teifi, Gwili and Tywi, including Ystrad Tywi and the west of Carmarthenshire; approximate area 2,284 km2

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no Dyfed (its Brythons rows cover Wales). The infobox gives 'Established: c. 410'. Pembrokeshire plus all Carmarthenshire is about 3,200 km2, above the infobox 2,284 km2 (ratio 1.4, inside the factor of two); the Ystrad Tywi part is the researcher's reading of the three rivers.

correction.text: Dyfed without Ystrad Tywi, which it 'lost ... to Ceredigion, another petty kingdom, in the late 7th century': Pembrokeshire and western Carmarthenshire

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Pembrokeshire (1,619 km2) plus the 20 km circle is about 2,900 km2 against the infobox 2,284 km2 (ratio 1.3). Seven cantrefi are listed on the page.

region.text: Dyfed on the territory of the Demetae

ledger.note: c. 410: Dyfed emerges in sub-Roman Britain. 'one of several petty kingdoms that emerged in 5th-century sub-Roman Britain in southwest Wales'; infobox 'Established: c. 410'; 'The royal line was founded by Irish settlers in the 5th century'.

Late 7th century: Dyfed loses Ystrad Tywi. 'Dyfed lost the Ystrad Tywi region to Ceredigion, another petty kingdom, in the late 7th century.' 690 is a rounding (confidence 1); Ceredigion became Seisyllwg in 680 (Seisyllwg page).

920: Dyfed becomes part of Deheubarth. 'In 920 Hywel merged Seisyllwg with the Kingdom of Dyfed to form the new kingdom of Deheubarth.' The Dyfed page has Hywel incorporate Dyfed through his marriage to Elen, heiress after Llywarch ap Hyfaidd died about 904, and its infobox gives 'Disestablished: 920'.

wars.name: Viking raids on Dyfed
wars.outcome: 'Dyfed was subject to extensive raids during the Viking Age between the 8th and 11th centuries'; in 999 a Viking raiding party attacked St Davids and killed Bishop Morganau.

certainty.note: The page gives rivers, cantrefi and an area, no boundary.

sources.title: Kingdom of Dyfed
sources.note: Identity, 410-920, extent, area, Ystrad Tywi, Viking raids.

notes: The page names no capital (Narberth is not on it), so capitals is empty. Dyfed under Norman rule (1068-1100, Pembrokeshire by 1138) belongs to the Deheubarth and marcher-lordship dossiers. The Dyfed page and the Seisyllwg page disagree on when Hywel took Dyfed (marriage after 904 versus the 920 merger); 920 is the infobox end. Eu-11-a asked for a 'dyfed' dossier 540-1100; the page's span is 410-920.
